title: I gave an LLM agent my Robinhood account for 3 months. Screenshots from my app and from Robinhood.
author: murdocc007
selftext:
Been building this a few months and finally have enough of a track record to post about it without feeling like a fraud.

The idea: instead of coding a strategy, you write it as a paragraph. Mine is literally "Buy and hold quality companies at fair prices. Long-term focus." That's the whole thing. The agent wakes up every 4 hours, looks at its positions, cash, quotes and recent news, and decides whether to buy, sell, or do nothing. Most of the time it does nothing, which surprised me.

It's mostly paper trading. You make an agent, it gets $100k fake, and there's a feed and a leaderboard where you can read the reasoning behind every trade other people's agents make. Third screenshot is the leaderboard — every agent is scored against the S&P over the same window, because a big green number in a bull market means nothing on its own.

Then Robinhood shipped their agentic trading API and I hooked one agent up to a real account with $10k in it. First two screenshots are my app and the Robinhood app showing the same balance. Up 6.61% in about three months.

Before anyone gets excited: one account, three months, a bullish stretch. I'd guess it's about the same as buying SPY and going outside. Three months of one agent isn't a result, it's an anecdote with screenshots. The leaderboard numbers are paper fills with no slippage or spread, so real fills are worse. I know they're worse, I'd rather say it than have it be the top comment.

Things I didn't expect to have to build:

* A restricted ticker list, because the first thing you learn with real money is you cannot let a language model touch your employer's stock
* Options and futures blocked in code, not in the prompt. Telling a model "don't do X" is not a control
* Idempotency on every order. Retry logic plus a trading API is a bad combination and I found that out the polite way in paper mode

If you want to try it: [**wallstreetclaws.com**](http://wallstreetclaws.com) is free, paper only, no card. You're building an agent in about a minute. Real-money trading runs through the [desktop app](https://wallstreetclaws.com/desktop) (mac + windows, still beta). Robinhood puts agents in a separate sub-account, so your main portfolio isn't reachable even if my code does something stupid.

Happy to answer anything about how it works.

I built this so I'm biased. Not advice. Don't put money you need into anything a language model is driving.

comments.author: FaithlessnessFit2900
comments.body: Does it have some prebuilt strategies I can use?

replies.author: murdocc007
replies.body: Yeah, six presets(https://prnt.sc/sqNOGsa3OSX1): Patient Value Investor, Momentum Trader, High Conviction Yolo, Dividend & Safety First, Contrarian Value Hunter, and Sector ETF Rotator. You pick one and it loads a starting prompt you can then read and edit — it's not a black box, it's just English you can argue with.

replies.author: FaithlessnessFit2900
replies.body: They are all fully agentic.. do you have plans to do quant strategies as well? Using indicators, entry conditions, exit conditions, etc?

replies.author: murdocc007
replies.body:
Working on implementing infra for quant strategies which will enable serious traders to backtest as well as run it in live environment.

About entry and exit conditions as of today you can just specify in the prompt and agent should ideally adhere to your constraints.

comments.author: jamesdal1
comments.body: How do you"give" it to the LLM?

replies.author: murdocc007
replies.body:
You can do this yourself if you want. Grab the desktop app from [wallstreetclaws.com/desktop](http://wallstreetclaws.com/desktop) and connect your own Robinhood account. It's Robinhood's own login, I never see a password, and agents run in a separate sub-account you fund yourself so it can't touch your main portfolio.

Or try it on paper on the site first, that's free and takes a minute.

replies.author: jamesdal1
replies.body: Can you use your own LLM

replies.author: murdocc007
replies.body: We use gemini based agents as of right now. But we can certainly adding your llms in the future.

comments.author: oskar88895
comments.body: Lmao 6% in 3 months, what is this

replies.author: murdocc007
replies.body:
This is just a single strategy, you can look at the paper trading results of some other strategies: https://wallstreetclaws.com/leaderboard which have been performing quite well.
If you don't want to play with real money you can try out paper trading agents.
Anyways, I didn't claim that these agents are going to beat s&p but we are working towards making them better.
